findings.issue: House rule is search phrase, then one plain sentence, then hashtags. This is two sentences plus a save-this tail, which reads longer than the format allows.
findings.fix: Cut to one sentence, e.g. "A cell reference inside quotes is just text to Excel, so put it outside and join it on with ampersands." Drop or shorten the save-this tail.

findings.issue: Third reel whose hook is a zero result (002 "totals zero", 012 "0.00 and nothing was ever reported"). The situation is genuinely new but the shape of the hook line is getting familiar.
findings.fix: Lead on the mismatch rather than the number, e.g. "Two CINTAS payments. COUNTIF says none." Keeps the symptom, changes the shape.

findings.where: script[5] caption "Excel looked for A2 itself."
findings.issue: "itself" is doing vague work; the point is Excel searched the memos for the two characters A and 2.
findings.fix: Try "Excel searched for the text A2." over "Move A2 out of the quotes."

findings.where: script[8] "every vendor gets a real count"
findings.issue: COUNTIF counts memo rows that contain the name, not occurrences of the name. Fine for this data, slightly loose as a general statement.
findings.fix: Optional: "every vendor gets its memo count" or leave as is since the sheet has one hit per row.

hook.note: Concrete, specific, a thing a controller has actually seen when tying a bank feed to a vendor list. Under 10 on-screen words. Loses a point only because the zero-result framing has been used twice before on this channel.

claims.claim: A cell reference inside quotes is treated as literal text, so "*A2*" searches for the characters A2
claims.note: Correct. COUNTIF criteria is a text string; A2 inside quotes is never resolved as a reference.

claims.claim: None of the four memos contain the text A2, so the count is 0
claims.note: Consistent with the data and the verified expected value.

claims.claim: Asterisks still work as wildcards when concatenated outside the quotes
claims.note: COUNTIF applies wildcard matching to the assembled criteria string regardless of how it was built.
Rows 7 and 9 both contain CINTAS. Matches the verified value.

claims.claim: Fill down gives GRAINGER 1 and FEDEX 1
claims.note: Range is absolute, criteria reference is relative, one matching memo each.
COUNTIF, wildcards and ampersand concatenation all work in 2016 and 2019.

claims.claim: Payoff "Inside the quotes, A2 is just two characters"
claims.note: Accurate and repeatable to a coworker.
